text:
Maya Chen: Quick heads-up — rollout 2026.03.23-rc2 finished to prod at 14:03 UTC. Our post-release quickchecks show a short burst of 502s from the inference-proxy in us-east-1 between ~14:04-14:06.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot reporting: post-deploy quickchecks for 2026.03.23-rc2 — observed 502 spike (~0.8% error rate over 2m) on route /v1/generate. Rolling update not fully finished (≈95% done).

Jin Park: looking at traces now — errors correlate with proxy -> model-router timeouts (backend timed out), not CPU/GPU OOMs on model hosts. Sample trace id: trace-0a3f9c (showing `upstream_timeout`).

Carlos Vega: Can we lock the model version for the route (avoid variant selector changes) while we triage? Something like:
`rbctl pin --service inference --route /v1/generate --model redwood-7b-quant@v2.14.1`
But if it's proxy->router timeouts, pinning may be orthogonal.

Priya Nair: Agree pinning might not help if proxy->router is the failing hop. Alternative quick mitigation: divert remaining rollout traffic for this route to the dedicated pool in us-east-1 and run extended quickchecks before finishing rollout.

Maya Chen: We have two options now:
A) Abort/rollback the release to 2026.03.22-stable (safer, preserves SLA)
B) Lock model versions + divert remaining traffic to dedicated pool and continue rollout after extra checks.
Holding decision — what do ops/oncall think? @Jin @Priya

Jin Park: I prefer rollback. Lower blast radius and meets latency SLA. Also recommend we run an expanded synthetic exercise that reproduces batched requests at p95 (seq_len 256) before reattempting.

deploy-bot: Action logged: rollback requested by @Jin Park. Rolling back 2026.03.23-rc2 -> 2026.03.22-stable. Rollback started at 14:17 UTC, will post status updates here.

ops-bot: Runbook triggered: start targeted synthetic sweep in us-east-1 to validate rollback health: `./scripts/synth-sweep --route /v1/generate --ramp 100qps --batch-sim 32 --duration 5m` — monitoring dashboards: /dashboards/infra/postrelease-quickcheck

Priya Nair: After rollback completes, capture detailed traces from the proxy and router for the failed hostset. Proposal: add hard quickcheck invariant -> fail the release if proxy 5xx > 0.3% sustained over 5m. Will file a patch for the quickcheck config.

Maya Chen: Thanks. I've put a short note in release notes and pinged #support with the rollback summary. I'll open a follow-up postmortem thread and assign initial owners for tracer collection and quickcheck patch.
__note: This thread represents a short deploy coordination exchange about a post-release verification anomaly and the decision to rollback. Messages are chronological and formatted as Slack-style inline messages.
